raw_case_text: Case 9: A 25 year old patient that reported exanthema and pruritus in the third trimester of gestation. Her IgM serology was positive for Zika and the PRNT90% was positive for neutralizing antibodies. At 37 weeks of gestation, her baby girl was born by cesarean with a cephalic circumference of 27 cm. The placenta weighed 565 g.

subjective.chief_complaint: 25-year-old pregnant female in the third trimester of gestation presenting with exanthema and pruritus.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient developed an acute pruritic exanthema during the third trimester of gestation. At 37 weeks of gestation, she delivered a baby girl by cesarean section who was found to have severe microcephaly.
subjective.past_medical_history: Third trimester of pregnancy; no prior chronic medical conditions reported.

objective.physical_examination: Maternal: Cutaneous exanthema. Neonatal: Female infant delivered at 37 weeks gestation by cesarean section with a cephalic circumference of 27 cm (severe microcephaly). Placental weight was 565 g.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Congenital Zika syndrome with severe neonatal microcephaly following maternal third-trimester Zika virus infection. Maternal infection was confirmed by positive Zika IgM serology and positive PRNT90% neutralizing antibodies. The infant girl was delivered at 37 weeks gestation with severe microcephaly (head circumference 27 cm; placental weight 565 g).
